headline: Histology guides recovery of unmeasured gene expression in 2D and 3D spatial transcriptomics
label: Histology Anchored Spatial Expression Reconstruction
summary: New preprints use histology to extend sparse spatial transcriptomics into continuous 3D fields, 1,000-gene panels, and single-cell profiles.
synthesis: The dominant thread treats histology as a scaffold for recovering expression that was not measured. HIM-INR and HoloGene use implicit neural representations to estimate continuous 3D gene-expression fields from sparse or pre-registered sliced spatial transcriptomics. GeneFlow applies flow matching with histology and gene tokenizers to predict panels of up to 1,000 genes, and CroSP fuses expression, location and histology through cross-view contrastive graph learning. Related work refines resolution: st2sc infers single-cell profiles from multicellular spots and SpaAxFormer imputes expression with axial transformers. multiCAsp adds a spatial prior to multi-omic analysis. SCALEMAP and GatorAnchor address non-spatial multi-omics integration, and scOntoFM embeds cell ontology hierarchy in a single-cell foundation model.
